title: 1031 Exchange Deadlines: 45-Day and 180-Day Rules Explained
summary: Missed 1031 exchange deadlines can trigger tax liability. Learn how the 45-day and 180-day rules work and how to protect your exchange.
body_text: A successful 1031 exchange requires more than selecting the right replacement property. Missing an IRS deadline may result in losing your tax deferral. Understanding 1031 exchange deadlines helps preserve capital, maintain your transaction timeline, and avoid costly mistakes before closing. 1031 Exchange Deadlines: 45-Day and 180-Day Rules Two deadlines define every exchange: Identifying the replacement property within 45 days. Completing the acquisition within 180 days. Both periods run simultaneously. Investors have 45 days to identify replacement property and must complete the exchange within 180 calendar days of the transfer or closing date of the relinquished property, or by the tax return due date, including extensions, if earlier. The 45-day window is often the most challenging, as it starts immediately after the transfer or closing date of the relinquished property. Market competition, financing delays, due diligence findings, and negotiations can limit options, making early planning critical. Weekends and holidays count toward both deadlines, so investors should avoid waiting until the last days to identify or close on replacement property. These deadlines generally can’t be extended, except in limited circumstances such as IRS relief for federally declared disasters. A compressed timeline can hinder evaluation of long-term investment suitability. How Identification Works Under 1031 Exchange Deadlines Investors must submit a written, signed notice within 45 days that clearly describes each replacement property by address, legal description, or another specific identifier. Verbal discussions or vague descriptions are insufficient. Written identification should follow the qualified intermediary’s required process, clearly describe the property, and be properly documented and delivered before the deadline. You can identify properties using: Three-property rule : Identify up to three potential replacement properties, regardless of value. 200% rule : Identify more than three properties if their combined fair market value doesn’t exceed 200% of the relinquished property’s fair market value. 95% rule : Identify any number of properties if you ultimately acquire identified replacement property with a fair market value of at least 95% of the aggregate fair market value of all identified replacement properties. Identifying backup properties helps reduce deal risk, especially when a preferred replacement property faces competitive bidding, financing issues, or due diligence concerns. How the 180-Day Rule Affects Closing Strategy Investors must complete the replacement property acquisition within 180 days of transferring the relinquished property, or by the taxpayer’s return due date, including extensions, if earlier. Because this period includes the 45-day identification window, they have limited time to finalize financing, complete due diligence, negotiate terms, and close. Closing delays pose significant risks. Title issues, lender requirements, environmental reviews, appraisals, or negotiations can push the transaction close to the deadline. If the acquisition is not completed on time, the exchange may fail even if the property was properly identified. Investors should consider how the 180-day period aligns with tax filing deadlines. Depending on the sales date, a tax return extension may be necessary to preserve the full exchange period. Early involvement of tax advisors is recommended. Why the Qualified Intermediary Matters Successful exchanges depend on an independent party that holds sale proceeds, provides required documentation, and helps ensure funds aren’t treated as received by the investor. Specific criteria apply when selecting a qualified intermediary. Investors should discuss these requirements with a trusted advisor to understand how they may affect the exchange structure. If an investor receives or has actual or constructive control of sale proceeds at any time, the transaction may become taxable. Engaging a qualified intermediary before closing is critical, as the exchange structure must be established before funds are disbursed. For more on structuring requirements, revisit 1031 Exchange Rules: What Real Estate Leaders Need to Know . Common Deadline Mistakes to Avoid Execution problems often arise before investors recognize a risk. Common mistakes include waiting until after closing to search for replacement property, assuming the identification period can be extended, or relying solely on a preferred property without backup. Other risks include incomplete property descriptions, overlooked financing constraints, lack of coordination with the qualified intermediary, or underestimating the time needed for due diligence and closing. These issues are difficult to correct once deadlines begin. A strong strategy should start before the relinquished property closes, with clear plans for property identification, financing and advisor coordination. What Clients Should Consider Meeting 1031 exchange deadlines requires coordination across several moving parts: Financing terms and lender timing Property sourcing and backup options Due diligence, inspections and title review Exchange documentation and intermediary coordination You should also evaluate: Gain exposure Cash needs Replacement property availability Entity structure Tax return filing deadlines and extension needs Whether identified properties align with the investor’s long-term strategy A practical approach includes engaging a qualified intermediary before closing, identifying replacement properties early, confirming financing, preparing backup options, and coordinating tax, legal, and real estate advisors before the 45-day window begins. Don’t Miss Critical Deadlines A successful exchange starts well before closing. Work with a CBIZ advisor early to meet critical deadlines, document your exchange correctly, and evaluate property options before time runs short. Frequently Asked Questions Investors must identify potential replacement property within 45 calendar days after the transfer or closing date of the relinquished property and complete the acquisition within 180 calendar days, or by the taxpayer’s return due date, including extensions, if earlier. These timelines run at the same time, not consecutively, and weekends and holidays count. Missing the 45-day identification deadline generally disqualifies the exchange. The IRS may treat the transaction as a taxable sale, meaning the investor could owe capital gains tax, depreciation recapture, and any applicable state taxes in the year of the sale. Standard business delays, financing issues, weekends, and holidays typically don’t extend the deadline, except in limited circumstances such as IRS relief for federally declared disasters. Investors should identify replacement properties early and confirm documentation with their qualified intermediary before the 45-day window closes. Investors can identify more than three potential replacement properties during the 45-day identification period if the combined fair market value of those properties doesn’t exceed 200% of the relinquished property’s fair market value. This rule gives investors more flexibility when evaluating multiple replacement options, but they must document the identified properties properly before the deadline. © Copyright CBIZ, Inc. title: 29 Sprout Social features you might not know about
summary: Take a closer look at 29 impactful Sprout Social features for brands, from AI-powered agents to predictive media monitoring tools.
body_text: Table of Contents Share Email Share Resource Sprout Social features are designed to help you move at the speed of social. Instead of juggling disconnected tools, Sprout offers teams a centralized system where they can gather social insights, learn from live audience behavior and act across areas like publishing, influencer marketing, customer care and crisis response. But Sprout goes beyond social media management, delving deeper into the realm of social intelligence. The AI-powered platform enriches CRM and BI systems with real‑time sentiment, cultural context and predictive analyses. The result? A comprehensive customer journey that explores what people are thinking, feeling and doing right now—and where those conversations are headed next. In this article, we’re highlighting Sprout Social features you might not know about. These tools help teams turn real-time social signals into smart, strategic business decisions. What does Sprout Social do? Sprout Social is an AI-powered social intelligence platform, backed by the belief that all business is social. With Trellis, Sprout’s proprietary AI agent, the platform translates real-time social media trends and signals into actionable business insights. With a suite of solutions across publishing, engagement, analytics, social listening, customer care, influencer marketing, advocacy and media monitoring, Sprout empowers brands to make smarter moves across all major social networks and drive stronger business impact. Try Sprout for free Sprout AI features AI and automation is embedded across Sprout’s entire platform, enabling your team to unlock creativity while increasing social media’s business impact. By automating data curation and analysis, these capabilities empower you to turn passive data into immediate action. 1. Turn social data into strategic decisions with Trellis, Sprout’s agentic AI When you’re wading through a sea of metrics, it’s difficult to zoom out and see the big picture of what’s working, what’s not and how to adjust your tactics accordingly. That’s where Trellis comes in. Simply ask it a question, and it queries billions of data points to return executive-ready intelligence. For instance, Trellis can help you break down a trend. Say you submit the query “Where did it start (e.g., niche subreddit, TikTok subculture)? Is it a “Micro-trend” (fleeting), a “Macro-trend” (seasonal) or a “Cultural Shift” (permanent change in behavior)?” In a matter of seconds, Trellis will use its social listening abilities to generate engagement trends, sentiment shifts and audience signals. Better still, it will translate those insights into actionable recommendations you can apply to your next campaign—bridging the gap between raw signals and business impact. 2. Automate your analyses with Trellis Studio Trellis Studio automates your recurring social analyses. It also uses pre-set conversation starters—known as skills—to ensure your team stays abreast of key performance and audience insights. For example, you could create a ‘Generate Post Ideas’ skill to support social content ideation. You can then customize this skill, choosing your preferred cadence, data sources and topics (if applicable). When that skill runs, you’ll receive a notification. By clicking on the alert, you’ll open a new Trellis Chat with details on the analysis. Rather than reactively searching for data, you can rely on Trellis Studio’s proactive approach. Set it and have social intelligence insights delivered directly to your inbox. 3. Keep your messaging fresh and on brand with AI Assist Sprout’s AI Assist is built into every part of the platform, optimizing everyday activities from content creation to engagement and customer care. For example, Generate by AI Assist produces alt text suggestions to increase the accessibility of your image-focused posts. With it, a previously tedious task is handled in seconds—a level of convenience Sprout customers love. “The AI alt text for images is extremely helpful,” says Jarod , Social Media Coordinator at The Born Group. “It saves me a bunch of time thinking of that and creates less work for me.” There’s also Enhance by AI Assist, which lets you choose from four different stylistic tones in the Smart Inbox. Draft a message, select your desired tone and the tool will tailor it accordingly. By keeping your messaging consistent and on brand, you’ll preserve brand credibility and foster trust while enabling your care team to scale their social media customer service . Sprout Social publishing features You can find everything you need to develop, manage and optimize your posts across all major platforms in Sprout’s Publishing. If you want to streamline your publishing workflow, try these must-know Sprout Social features. 4. Share critical context with Calendar Notes Picture this: You know a major promotion or event is coming, but you haven’t received the details needed to craft the perfect post. Now, your publishing calendar has several blank spots you know you’re holding for the promotion—but no one else does. Calendar Notes democratize that information by acting as a placeholder in your Publishing Calendar. This prevents your colleagues from scheduling additional content because they see a gap in your publishing queue. It also gives business leaders a more accurate view of your publishing cadence. You can use Calendar Notes to share ideas with your team, or to share reminders to amplify content from influencers and business partners. 5. Schedule directly from your browser with the Sprout browser extension If you rely on curating industry-specific news to boost thought leadership on your brand’s social accounts, you need to use the Sprout Social browser extension . This tool brings the Compose Window with you as you browse the web for relevant articles to share. When you find something that would appeal to or intrigue your audience, simply click on the extension to add it to your Sprout Queue. 6. Drive Instagram traffic with SproutLink Link in bio tools empower marketers to promote as many links as their strategy demands on Instagram, but there are trade-offs. For example, jumping between a social media management tool, a link in bio tool and Instagram to make sure everything is consistent can quickly become a tedious task. That’s why we created SproutLink. SproutLink consolidates your Instagram publishing workflow by creating posts, managing and reporting on associated links all within Sprout Social. SproutLink creates a clickable version of your Instagram grid that gives your audience more content choices and ways to explore your brand. 7. Keep content production on track with External Approvals Sprout’s Message Approval workflow is a game-changer for social media teams navigating multi-step content review processes. But did you know it’s not limited to individuals with seats in Sprout? Brands using the Sprout Social Advanced Plan can add external approvers simply by adding the individual’s email address to their Message Approval workflow. Once the user verifies their email address, they can review assigned posts, provide feedback and give their stamp of approval. Plus, Sprout will send external approvers automated reminder emails leading up to their deadline if an approval hasn’t come through yet. This not only saves time and effort, but it alleviates the common pain point of remembering to follow up. 8. Use Custom Variables to manage posts across multiple profiles When managing multiple social profiles, you may want to include unique locations or URLs across different networks. For example, you may want to use URLs with UTM codes tailored to each network so you can seamlessly track where your site traffic is coming from. That process is made simple with Sprout’s Custom Variables. Create up to 10 custom variables for networks like Facebook, Instagram Business, LinkedIn and TikTok. Once set up, you can simply insert the dynamic variable into your posts—making it easy to adapt your content across networks without the extra manual effort. 9. Easily customize content posted across different networks While it’s common to publish the same content across multiple networks, each has its own requirements and constraints, such as caption character limits and image dimensions. With Sprout’s Network Preview, you can see exactly how your post will look across networks. You can then toggle back and forth between channels and make adjustments in the composer, tweaking copy, tags or visuals. Instead of jumping between native schedulers and guessing how each network will format your content, you can make all your customizations in one place. According to small business owner, Jon , this is one of Sprout’s top traits: “The most helpful aspect of Sprout Social is its ability to publish posts across multiple social media platforms. I can customize each scheduled post to meet the specific standards of each platform and tailor the content to fit each account.” Sprout Social engagement & customer care features On social media, engagement is everything—it’s how you connect, support and build relationships with your target audience. With Sprout, you can scale these engagements as you grow. Use the features below to help your team spot high-priority conversations, jump in when customers need help and deliver the right tone in every response. 10. Moderate and engage in owned subreddits on Reddit With Sprout’s Reddit integration you have the ability to connect moderated subreddits and user profiles to your account. When you link a subreddit, Sprout will pull posts and comments from that specific forum into the Smart Inbox. You can then use your user profile to engage with that content, whether it’s replying, upvoting, hiding or deleting posts. With this integration, it’s far easier to stay in touch with the communities you own in one place. You can review Reddit activity, respond faster and keep threads appropriate without bouncing between platforms. 11. Keep customer data safe with data masking and secure forms Guardian by Sprout Social takes the guesswork and intimidation out of compliance . By offering enterprise-grade control functions, it provides your team with the power to execute social strategy and build trust at scale. One way it does this is by protecting users’ personally identifiable information (PII). For instance, Predefined Data Masking identifies and masks sensitive information—like phone number, email address or credit card number—from networks like Facebook, Instagram, X, WhatsApp and LinkedIn. Sprout’s Secure Forms also enable you to handle sensitive queries and collect PII and protected health information (PHI) in a PCI-compliant way without having to leave the platform. 12. Revisit social customer care activity and conversations with Contact Profile Views One of the most unique Sprout Social features is Contact Profile Views, which provide a peek into customers’ social media activity. Using this view, you can see users’ behaviors and also add custom contact notes, reply to their messages and see message history between you and the individual. Contact Profile Views are available on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and X. These views give you a more human look at the people you’re trying to sell to, support and connect with. Social activity, past interactions and internal notes create invaluable context as to who’s on the other side of the screen. Your team can then use these details to personalize responses and maintain consistent care. 13. Automatically complete @mentions only comments While followers tagging their friends in a comment boost your brand’s visibility, these comments can crowd your Inbox. To save time, you can enable Complete @mention Comments in Sprout’s Inbox Settings. Little tools like these make a big difference when it comes to reducing the amount of noise going on in your social media inbox. Less noise means social customer care agents can stay focused on the messages that matter most. 14. Automatically complete @mentions only comments Sprout’s AI-powered sentiment analysis tools help marketers and customer service agents monitor brand health in both messages and reviews, which improves efficiency and mitigates risk. Creating a custom inbox view based on negative sentiment will give you a bird’s-eye view of the less-than-glowing feedback your business has received within a given time period. It’s not always fun to look at, but it’s a crucial way to keep an eye on potential social media crises . If several complaints share similar themes, you can also use this intel to pitch necessary customer experience improvements to the rest of your team. Sprout Social reporting & analytics features Reporting is often the most important—and most time-consuming—aspect of a social media manager’s job. Consolidating several network-specific metrics into one comprehensive report without a sophisticated reporting tool can take hours, if not days. Sprout’s reporting and analytics tools are designed to help users uncover the deeper why behind performance and craft compelling stories with that data. The following Sprout Social features make quantifying the impact of your social media performance easy: 15. Track KPIs that matter most to your business with Custom Metrics Sprout’s Custom Metrics enable you to create, manage and apply your own formulas across post-level reporting. To create one, simply use basic mathematical functions (e.g. +, -, ×, ÷) in combination with existing post-level metrics. You can also apply Custom Metrics to specific networks or across all channels. Custom Metrics give you a closer look at important KPIs and make it easier to cut through the sea of stats touncover the performance signals that drive real business impact. 16. Keep stakeholders informed with scheduled PDF reports Automating report delivery is an easy way to take a recurring task off your to-do list. With Sprout, you can schedule reports to send to up to 25 people weekly or monthly. Customers with our Premium Analytics add-on can easily share reports with anyone using direct links, even if they don’t have a Sprout account. These links update automatically, strengthening alignment between teams and internal stakeholders. 17. Get granular insights with Tagging Tags are a game-changing Sprout feature that helps marketers group and categorize posts for flexible reporting on content by theme, type, campaign—the opportunities really are endless. For more detailed reporting options, we recommend setting up Tag Collections. These let you organize Tags with similar themes. For example, a retail brand might set up a customer support Tag Collection that groups all of their issue-specific Tags, like “Shipping Delay”, “Damaged Product” and “Negative In-Store Experience”. You can analyze Collections and drill down into specific Tags within Collections using the Tag Performance Report. This report offers easy-to-follow data visualizations and post-level insights that demystify the performance of tagged posts and messages. 18. Expand your reporting capabilities with My Reports If you want to truly maximize your social media reporting options, then you need My Reports, available in Sprout’s Premium Analytics tool. With My Reports, you can build customizable reports complete with multiple tables and dynamic visualizations—like bar and line charts—to compare performance across a number of networks. Filtering options allow teams to go broad to granular in just a few clicks, sorting data by metric, Tag, content type and more. Once you’ve organized the data to your liking, you can add critical context using annotation widgets that are perfect for executive summaries and miscellaneous notes. All these tools work together to help teams understand social’s impact at a glance, in a format that resonates. Sprout Social Listening features Social Listening is a Sprout Social premium solution that allows brands to uncover trends and actionable insights from social. This AI-powered tool scales the process of premium data ingestion, delivering actionable insights needed to guide your future strategy. Because Listening is a premium add-on, trial accounts don’t have access to the tool. However, you can still see it in action by scheduling a demo . If you do, here are three features to ask about: 19. Focus on the most relevant discussions with Sprout’s advanced Reddit listening With Sprout, your team can cut through Reddit noise and focus on the forums that matter for your brand. Its tools enable you to isolate key subreddits, filter out high‑noise communities and track every single post from your most critical communities. In turn, you get cleaner listening data, sharper sentiment insights and complete confidence that you’re capturing the full context of how people perceive your brand, even when they don’t mention you by name. 20. Reduce unnecessary noise with spam filtration Spam posts on social media are like taxes or traffic jams—they’re annoying, but inevitable. That’s why it’s important to invest in tools that tune them out. Sprout Social’s Listening tool has built-in filtering technology that excludes common noise categories like sweepstakes, sales listings, coupons and adult content. If your Listening Topic is pulling spam messages that don’t fall into those categories, you can set up custom filtration options using the spam publisher’s location or website information. These tools increase the accuracy of your listening data, so you’re left with insights driven by real people—not bots. 21. Get real-time alerts when conversation volume spikes Stay ahead of unexpected conversation surges with Listening Spike Alerts. These real-time notifications automatically flag significant increases in message volume within your Listening topics, so you can respond quickly to emerging trends, viral moments or potential issues. Customize alert thresholds based on your brand’s baseline activity to ensure you’re only notified when it matters most. Whether it’s a sudden influx of customer feedback, a PR moment gaining traction or a competitor making headlines, Spike Alerts help you act fast and stay informed—without having to constantly monitor dashboards. Spike Alerts are delivered via email and integrated into your Smart Inbox, keeping your team connected to the moments that matter most. Sprout Social influencer marketing & advocacy features Sprout Social Influencer Marketing and Employee Advocacy by Sprout Social enable authentic brand amplification. The former gives you the tools to find the right creators, manage partnerships with ease and measure the impact of your campaigns. The latter empowers employees to share brand content while staying compliant with pre-approved copy. From discovery to reporting, these features help you scale your program and drive meaningful results. 22. Evaluate creators with confidence using Brand Safety and Brand Fit Score Protect your brand reputation before partnerships begin with Brand Safety, a feature that scans public posts from the past year and assigns a risk level based on customizable criteria. Sprout Social Influencer Marketing includes a set of default safety categories, which include alcohol, adult content, gambling and more. Admins have the power to customize these rules or add new ones to reflect brand-specific sensitivities. Additionally, the Brand Fit Score gives creators a percentage score based on how well their content aligns with your messaging and values. At a glance, you can assess which influencers to prioritize for your campaigns. Whether you’re working with creators at scale or navigating high-stakes campaigns, Brand Safety and Brand Fit Score help you partner with peace of mind. 23. Build polished campaign summaries in minutes Influencer Marketing’s One-Sheet Builder automatically generates a polished, shareable snapshot of key campaign details, highlighting creator profile summaries, deliverables, performance metrics and more. With just a few clicks, you can customize your one-sheet and export it as a polished PDF to share with stakeholders or clients. Users can choose from one of five default templates or create a new One-Sheet from scratch. It’s a fast, effective way to communicate results, reinforce the value of your influencer strategy and keep teams aligned on what success looks like. 24. Execute creator payments within your campaign workflow Rather than using external payment channels, use compatible integrations to issue creator payments within Sprout. Whether you opt for Lumanu or PayPal, this solution offers complete visibility into your spend while assuring timely and accurate payment for your creators. For executives like Allison , that centralization is extremely beneficial: “I love that literally EVERYTHING you could need is easily available within the platform. You are able to vet influencers, keep in contact with them, exchange payments/contracts and everything in between!” 25. Automatically halt off-brand messages before employees share them Stop risky messaging in its tracks with Sprout’s Blocked Words feature. Admins can create lists of off-brand, unsafe or non-compliant words. Once set, any content that contains them will be blocked from dissemination. With quick and simple automation, you can maintain control of your brand’s social presence and protect its credibility. Sprout Social predictive media monitoring features NewsWhip by Sprout Social is an AI-powered media monitoring tool that tracks millions of real-time news and social signals. Backed by patented predictive algorithms, NewsWhip is designed to forecast which stories will drive attention next. These are its top features and how they can support your team: 26. Protect your brand with Trellis Monitoring Agent The Trellis Monitoring Agent is an always-on system that detects meaningful media shifts early. It then delivers analyst-quality updates on these trends so you can forecast developing issues with no manual effort. Given that news cycles move quicker than ever, this kind of automated tool is essential for keeping pace. Plus, with its structured, contextual updates, you won’t just keep up, you’ll stay ahead. 27. Stay on top of the latest trends and situations with Alerts NewsWhip enables real-time and scheduled alerts; both deliver important information from your searches to you via email or Slack. Alerts eliminate the need to jump into NewsWhip to manually review engagement spikes and emerging narratives. Instead, the most important updates land directly in your inbox. This model empowers teams to remain proactive, make timely decisions and respond faster. 28. Keep your team informed on the most important topics with Digests NewsWhip’s AI Digest gives you instant context on broad media coverage. Think of it as your fast lane to understanding what’s happening without compromising on accuracy or depth. You can set up weekly or daily digests, which will break down engagement data on specific topics. Like standard alerts, these summaries provide ultimate convenience because they get delivered straight to you. 29. Monitor how stories spread, gain traction and evolve across the internet NewsWhip’s predictive algorithms map the full trajectory of any narrative, so you can see the exact moment a conversation starts to shift or intensify. This early visibility empowers brands to intervene before backlash snowballs, addressing small-scale issues and protecting reputation while the story is still forming. According to one Sprout user , NewsWhip is “invaluable” for crisis management. “The ability to see engagement velocity—how quickly a story or narrative is spreading—gives us the early warning signals we need to assess the situation and mobilize our team before something escalates. It’s helped us move from reactive to proactive in high-pressure moments.” Experience these Sprout Social features firsthand With a system that marries comprehensive social media management with social intelligence, you can maximize business-wide impact. Sprout’s capabilities—including AI-powered technology and predictive insights—help you win today and build for tomorrow all at once. And you can experience many of these features for yourself, even if you’re not already a Sprout customer. Simply schedule a demo to see these features in action. Need a little more information before taking the leap? Consult our social media management buyer’s guide to learn more about how Sprout can help you unlock the full value of social. Frequently Asked Questions What are the main features of Sprout Social? Some of Sprout’s key features across its main capabilities include: Engagement: Smart Inbox, Message Tagging, Message Spike Alerts. Publishing: Advanced Post Scheduling, Multi-Profile Publishing, ViralPost® Send Time Optimization. Analytics: Post Performance Report, Social Network Reports, Tag Report. Influencer Marketing & Employee Advocacy: Brand Safety, Brand Fit Score, Blocked Words. Listening: Query Builder, Listener Insights, Listener Dashboards. title: KYC vs. AML: Understanding the Key Differences in Compliance
summary: KYC and AML serve different roles in compliance. Understand their key differences, how they work together, and why a unified compliance pipeline strengthens risk management.
body_text: Financial institutions and regulated businesses face increasing pressure to prevent financial crime while ensuring seamless customer experiences. Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) are two essential components of a robust compliance program. While they are often mentioned together, they play distinct roles in helping organizations prevent fraud, combat money laundering, and meet regulatory requirements. KYC focuses on verifying a customer’s identity and evaluating risk during onboarding, while AML encompasses the broader processes used to detect, prevent, and report suspicious financial activity throughout the customer relationship. Therefore, when combined, they create the foundation of a strong compliance framework that helps businesses meet regulatory requirements and build trust. In this article, we’ll break down the key differences between KYC and AML, explain how they work together, and discuss why integrating both into a unified compliance pipeline is essential for effective risk management. What Separates KYC From AML Compliance? Although Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) work closely together, they serve different purposes within a compliance program. KYC is primarily concerned with confirming a customer’s identity at the start of the relationship, while AML is an ongoing framework that detects, prevents, and reports suspicious financial activities throughout the customer lifecycle. Therefore, it is important for organizations to understand the key difference between them because regulators treat KYC and AML as separate compliance obligations. This is because an organization may have effective customer identification processes in place, but without continuous AML monitoring, it remains vulnerable to money laundering, terrorist financing, fraud, and regulatory sanctions. When implemented together, KYC and AML provide a comprehensive compliance framework that helps businesses manage risk and meet evolving regulatory requirements. Why Does KYC Accuracy Determine AML Strength? An effective AML program begins with accurate KYC. The quality of customer identity data collected during onboarding directly impacts an organization’s ability to assess risk, detect suspicious activity, and comply with regulatory requirements. Therefore, if customer information is inaccurate, incomplete, or fraudulent, AML control effectiveness is significantly reduced. Transaction monitoring systems depend on verified customer profiles to identify unusual behavior and flag potential money laundering risks. As a result, when those profiles are built on unreliable identity data, businesses may generate false positives, overlook genuine threats, or fail to detect suspicious activities altogether. This weakens the overall compliance program and increases the risk of financial crime and regulatory penalties. For fintechs, financial institutions, and other regulated businesses, effective KYC practices lay the foundation for a successful AML compliance program. What Does a Unified Compliance Pipeline Look Like? A unified compliance pipeline integrates KYC, AML, KYB, identity verification, and risk monitoring into a single, connected workflow. Rather than organizations having to rely on multiple disconnected tools, they can manage customer onboarding, compliance checks, and ongoing risk assessments from one centralized platform. This minimizes operational complexity, improves data consistency, and enables compliance teams to respond to risks more efficiently. Without an integrated approach, organizations often struggle with fragmented customer data, duplicated processes, and limited visibility across their compliance operations. These gaps can slow onboarding, increase operational expenses, and make it more difficult to identify suspicious behavior or demonstrate compliance during regulatory audits. Platforms like Prembly streamline compliance by bringing identity verification, KYC, KYB, AML screening, background checks, and fraud prevention together within a single, unified infrastructure. With a single source of truth for customer risk data, businesses can streamline compliance operations, strengthen fraud detection, and support secure customer onboarding across multiple markets.

title: Mobile Observability: Real Teams, Real Fixes, and What Agentic AI Changes
summary: Mobile observability that acts, not just alerts. See how The Economist and Alinea closed the Action Gap with agentic AI.
body_text: TL;DR: For most mobile teams, mobile observability ends at the alert. Engineers handle everything after it, manually triaging stack traces, reproducing bugs, coordinating fixes across tools, and waiting on store review. Luciq's Agentic Mobile Observability platform closes that gap using AI agents that detect, triage, and resolve issues autonomously. At Mobile Observability: It's About Time (and Latency), engineering leaders from The Economist and Alinea Invest explained how they got there. Here's what they covered. Your on-call engineer gets the alert at 11:43 PM. A crash spike. Checkout flow. Android 14, carrier networks in the Northeast. They open the dashboard, scroll through stack traces, check the last three deploys, and ping the backend team. By 1:15 AM they have a likely cause. By Thursday, two days later, after QA, review, and App Store processing, there's a fix in users' hands. The investigation took ninety minutes. The fix took fifty-six hours to reach anyone. That gap between knowing something is wrong and actually resolving it is what Kenny Johnston, CPO at Luciq, calls the Action Gap. It is not a fluke. It is the architecture of how most mobile teams practice observability today. And for a long time, the industry has treated it (structurally) as something you manage, not something you fix. On April 16, 2026, Luciq hosted Mobile Observability: It's About Time (and Latency) , a half-day virtual event examining how agentic AI changes what it means to observe, understand, and act on mobile app performance. Three sessions. Real engineering leaders. A live platform walkthrough. Below is everything worth knowing, organized by session, with timestamped breakdowns of what was covered and why it matters. What Mobile Observability Actually Means in 2026 Mobile observability is the practice of collecting, analyzing, and acting on data that reflects how a mobile app behaves for real users: crashes, latency, network failures, UI errors, and the user interactions that connect them all. The definition has been stable for years. The execution, less so. For most teams, mobile observability still follows the same loop: a crash reporting tool fires an alert, an engineer investigates, a fix gets written, QA signs off, a release goes through store review. The whole cycle takes days. Users experience the problem the entire time. The observability part ends the moment the alert fires. Everything after it is manual. The Signal That Backend Tools Consistently Miss The four golden signals of observability - latency, traffic, errors, saturation - are well understood in backend engineering. Mobile adds a fifth signal that backend tools consistently miss: user experience context. What the user was doing. What they saw on screen. What sequence of events preceded the failure. Without that context, you have a stack trace. With it, you have a diagnosis. That distinction is where modern mobile application performance monitoring either earns its keep or does not. Session 1 | The State of Mobile: A Candid Conversation Kenny Johnston and Daniel Day covered the full picture: where mobile observability came from, where it is failing, and what the next version looks like. If you watch one session from this event, make it this one. What You Are Seeing in the Video The opening frame (0:00 to 3:18). Johnston and Day open by arguing that mobile apps are now the primary surface through which most brands interact with customers. Not websites. Not support calls. Apps. That framing matters because it raises the stakes on everything that follows. A checkout failure is not a mobile problem. It is a revenue problem. That reframe is worth sitting with before the rest of the conversation. The Action Gap, defined (4:10 to 7:50). This is the section worth rewinding. Johnston explains that web teams can push a fix in minutes - no intermediary, no review gating, direct to the user. Mobile teams do not have that. Store review cycles, manual triage, and release coordination mean the gap between detecting a problem and fixing it is measured in days. The industry has accepted this as a structural constraint. Johnston's argument is that it is a tooling failure, and that LLMs and automation have finally made it solvable. If your team still treats the next release as the earliest possible fix window, that assumption is worth interrogating. Context as the missing ingredient (8:45 to 14:00). Most mobile observability tools capture quantitative technical data: crash rates, error counts, network latency. Johnston argues this is roughly half the picture. The other half is qualitative - what the user was doing, what they experienced, what frustrated them before the crash happened. He breaks this into four categories: quantitative technical (crashes and logs), qualitative technical (bug reports), quantitative non-technical (product analytics and user flows), and qualitative non-technical (minor UI friction that never generates a ticket). When you blend all four, you stop prioritizing by volume and start prioritizing by impact. A crash affecting two hundred users in a checkout flow matters more than a cosmetic bug affecting ten thousand on a settings screen. The data to make that call exists. Most teams just are not assembling it in one place. Trust, governance, and AI adoption (14:45 to 19:15). Johnston outlines three principles Luciq holds for integrating agentic systems into engineering workflows. First: transparency, meaning on-device PII masking so sensitive user data never leaves the device. Second: Bring-Your-Own-Agent, integrating with the tools your team already uses - Cursor, Copilot, Claude - through standard interfaces like MCP servers and CLIs. Third: Human-in-the-Loop, meaning any action that touches production code or triggers a release requires a human approval step. These are not just product design decisions. They are the conditions under which engineering organizations will actually trust autonomous systems with real work. Where engineering time actually goes (22:45 to 23:30). Approximately sixty percent of mobile engineering time currently goes to maintenance: OS compatibility updates, regression fixes, quality issues generated by other people's changes. Johnston's goal is not incremental improvement on that number. It is flipping the ratio so engineers are building new experiences rather than keeping existing ones from breaking. Frustration-Free Sessions (28:00 to 30:30). The session closes with one of Luciq's core mobile app performance metrics : a scoring system that categorizes every user session as satisfying, tolerable, frustrating, or crashing, then assigns a business impact score to the issues driving the frustrating ones. The alternative most teams use is a spreadsheet, a crash-free rate, and a lot of judgment calls made on incomplete data. The Frustration-Free Session score does not replace engineering judgment. It replaces the manual work of assembling enough signals to exercise it. Session 2 | From the Trenches: Scaling Mobile Team Productivity Two engineering leaders from The Economist and Alinea Invest walked through what mobile observability looks like when the stakes are real. Subscription revenue. Financial transactions. Brands that depend on user trust. Luciq's Andrea Sy. hosted. What You Are Seeing in the Video Setting the stage (0:00 to 1:25). Anom McConnie is Co-founder of Alinea Invest, a fintech platform where performance is a trust signal. A slow transaction screen is not an inconvenience; it is a question mark next to a user's financial data. John Friend is Technical Team Lead at The Economist, a premium subscription product where app quality is brand quality. Neither company competes on price. Both compete on experience, which means every bad session has a cost that shows up somewhere other than an engineering dashboard. Why crash-free rate is not enough (3:56 to 4:28). Both guests make the same point from different angles. A 99% crash-free rate sounds healthy until you ask what the other one percent experienced, and whether the ninety-nine percent who did not crash were actually having a good time, or just a tolerable one. What both wanted was the full picture: session replay , system logs, memory and CPU usage, HTTP request data. Not just the what of a failure but the why behind it. As the Luciq blog has covered before, green dashboards can hide real damage , and both of these teams had experienced exactly that. The workflow integration that changes triage (8:04 to 12:07). Both companies connect Luciq to their existing stacks : Slack for real-time alerts , Jira and Linear for ticket creation, and New Relic for backend visibility. The piece that changes the game is not any single integration. It is the correlation. When a mobile crash and a backend API failure surface in the same timeline, the investigation collapses from hours to minutes. Engineers stop asking whether it is their problem or the backend's, and start looking at what actually happened. MTTR drops, and so does the cognitive overhead of cross-team debugging. Performance is a revenue metric (19:35 to 23:53). Both guests reframe app stability as a financial question rather than a quality one. Negative App Store reviews affect conversion. Poor stability drives uninstalls. According to Luciq's own research, 15.4% of users uninstall after a single crash . For a subscription product like The Economist, churn from a buggy experience is direct revenue loss. For a fintech app like Alinea, a transaction failure is a trust failure, and trust is the product. The question is not whether to invest in observability. It is whether you invest before or after users start leaving. What AI makes possible next (24:32 to 25:00 and 27:35 to 28:17). Both guests describe the capability they are most excited about: AI that identifies patterns before they become incidents. The shift from " we detected a spike " to " we noticed a cluster forming twelve hours ago and your users never felt it " is what proactive mobile observability looks like in practice. They described it as what they are building toward, and why they chose an agentic platform over a traditional monitoring stack. The panel's closing advice. Anom's take: keep shipping, keep fixing bugs: velocity and quality are not opposites. John's: put a bug report form in your app. Direct user feedback, enriched with automated context, is still one of the most actionable signals an engineering team can get. ‍ Session 3 | See It in Action: The Luciq Platform Live The third session is a hands-on walkthrough of the Luciq platform , tracing a real issue through every stage: detection, triage, resolution, and release. If you have ever wanted to see what agentic mobile observability looks like when it is actually running, this is the session. What You Are Seeing in the Video The SDK and the north star metric (0:33 to 2:59). The walkthrough opens with Luciq's SDK integration - lightweight, capturing crashes, OOM errors, ANR events, and network performance issues. The north star metric it feeds is the Frustration-Free Session Score : a single number synthesizing stability and performance data into a reflection of real user experience. Crash-free sessions only measure the worst-case outcome. The Frustration-Free Session Score measures everything before it. Agentic Triage (3:17 to 4:03) . Issues are automatically ranked by their impact on the Frustration-Free Session Score, not by raw occurrence count. A crash affecting twenty users in a checkout flow outranks a warning affecting two thousand on a low-stakes screen. Agentic Triage also groups duplicate user-submitted bug reports automatically , so one fix closes many tickets. Triage is often where the most experienced engineers spend the most time on work that generates the least value. This is what automating it looks like. Root cause analysis and the Resolve Agent (7:00 to 11:10). Stack traces, evidence patterns, and session context get analyzed together. The output is not "here are your logs." It is: here is what caused this, here is the user flow that triggered it, here is the code change that fixes it, and here is a draft pull request. The Resolve Agent can run CI/CD checks, merge the fix, and push a release to the App Store, with human approval required at any step the team's governance policy specifies. If you want to understand how this fits into a modern CI/CD for mobile workflow, that piece is worth reading alongside this one. MCP server and IDE integration (12:23 to 13:40). Developers who prefer to stay in their IDE can connect Luciq's MCP server to Cursor, Claude Code, or any MCP-compatible tool. Luciq's session data, root cause analysis, and reproduction steps become available directly inside the coding environment. No separate dashboard. No context switch. The information comes to the developer. Detection beyond crashes (14:30 to 17:02). One of the most practically important sections of the walkthrough covers what traditional crash reporting misses entirely: functional and visual bugs. Screens that require retries. Buttons that do not respond. API calls that fail silently and never generate a crash report, but do generate frustration, negative reviews, and uninstalls. The platform detects these patterns from session behavior, tags them automatically, and surfaces them with the session replay a developer needs to understand the failure. Beta testing support (19:04 to 20:00). The walkthrough closes with the beta testing workflow. A tester shakes their device or taps a floating button. The report automatically captures logs, device specs, and the full user flow. The developer receives a ticket that is already actionable, no follow-up required, no reproduction loop, no "can you share a screen recording?" The context that would normally take three back-and-forth exchanges to assemble is already there. What the Shift from Reactive to Agentic Actually Means for Your Team Mobile application performance monitoring has traditionally been organized around detection: find the problem, fire the alert, let engineers handle everything that follows. The engineering team becomes the resolution layer by default, which works when incidents are rare and teams are large, and breaks down when neither is true. Agentic mobile observability reorganizes that loop. Detection still happens. But triage, root cause analysis, fix generation, and release monitoring happen autonomously, with human approval at the decision points that actually warrant it. The result is not just a faster MTTR number. It is a different allocation of engineering attention. The Maintenance Math Is Hard to Ignore Mobile engineers currently spend roughly sixty percent of their time on maintenance work: OS upgrades, regression fixes, quality issues generated by other people's changes. Dabble, one of Luciq's customers in iGaming, cut their MTTR by fifty to sixty percent and reclaimed more than twenty engineering hours per week after making the shift, a story worth reading in full if you want to see the math play out in a real high-stakes environment. That is not an incremental improvement. That is a different way of operating. Luciq is the first and leading Agentic Mobile Observability platform . That is not category marketing. It is an architectural distinction: a single platform with unified context across the full maintenance lifecycle - detect , triage , fix , release - feeding agents that can act like a senior developer because they have access to the same data one would need. ‍ Watch all three sessions on demand , or bring the conversation to your team with a live platform walkthrough. Request a demo . Read next | Mobile Observability: What It Is and Why It Matters in the Age of AI

title: EA SPORTS™ College Football 27 brings the new era of College Football to life
summary: EA SPORTS™ College Football 27 launches worldwide on July 9, bringing the new era of college football to life.
body_text: EA SPORTS™ College Football 27 brings the new era of College Football to life Do it for u with 138 ways to play in Dynasty Mode, experience NIL and build your legacy in Road to Glory July 9, 2026 Today, we launched EA SPORTS™College Football 27 worldwide on PlayStation®5, Xbox Series X|S and, for the first time ever, PC and mobile. Following the record-breaking return of the franchise, College Football 27 raises the bar once again, delivering the most authentic college football experience yet. College Football 27 is the definitive modern college football experience. Every major change happening in the sport from NIL and coaching movement to recruiting, player development and game day is now reflected in the game at unprecedented scale. Built around the modern college football landscape, College Football 27 introduces the biggest changes to Dynasty Mode since the game's introduction, all-new dynamic weather, expanded Road to Glory positions and over 1,500 new plays, thousands of current athletes and more than 300 real coaches in the game. Whether building a powerhouse or creating a star rising through the ranks, every decision shapes a player’s legacy. “College football is experiencing an exciting and tension-filled transformation that has never been more compelling to watch. That tension is exactly what we wanted to reflect in College Football 27 - a duality of traditional school pride confronted by a dynamic athlete landscape," said Evan Dexter, VP of Franchise Strategy and Marketing. “The game doesn’t just reflect the modern era, it puts you at the center of it. Players will choose how they want to win and whether they’re in it for the campus traditions or the individual glory. Combined with incredible new gameplay innovation on the offensive and defensive sides of the ball, we can't wait for fans to experience a whole new season of drama, pride, rituals, and atmosphere on the sticks." Every mode in College Football 27 is inspired by today’s college football, from recruiting and roster building to game day traditions, with new gameplay systems giving players more control than ever before. Dynasty Mode Rebuilt: With 138 ways to build, the all-new Dynasty Blueprint system overhauls program management with playable NIL features, AD Expectations that put your job on the line, and Dynasty Points invested across facilities, recruiting, and staff. Soft commits can be flipped on signing day, while the Coaching Carousel lets you pursue any open job, putting you in the middle of the same decisions that define college football's most dramatic offseasons. More Like Saturday: Dynamic weather changes conditions over the course of a game, from first-quarter flurries to fourth-quarter whiteouts, while a refreshed broadcast package welcomes Joel Klatt to the booth and Holly Rowe to the sideline. New traditions, marching band songs, drone shows, livelier student sections and updated stadiums round out a genuine gameday atmosphere. Every Snap Matters: A new, optional timing-based catching system puts pass and interception outcomes directly in the player's hands, while smarter zone coverage logic and custom pre-play adjustments give players more tools than ever before on both sides of the ball. New Paths to Glory: Road to Glory expands with three new playable positions fans have been asking for: Edge Rusher, Free Safety, and Tight End. Each position comes with its own expectations and grading system. Revamped player lets you build your own athlete from scratch or step into the cleats of all-new Legend Builds, while a tracking system for on-and-off-field decisions shape draft stock and reputation resulting in Legacy Scores, which now carry over into Madden NFL 27's Superstar mode on draft day. The Fan Favorite is Back: Mascot Mashup, the community's most-requested mode, returns with over 100 unlockable mascots and chaotic 99 overall rated head-to-head matchups where every player is equal. Victory comes down to play calling, stick skills and making the most of the madness. EA SPORTS College Football 27 also marks the franchise's mobile debut, delivering the first-ever EA SPORTS College Football title powered by Frostbite. Available now on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, mobile players can dive into College Ultimate Team with more features coming soon. For more information, visit the official website and follow along on social media ( Instagram , X , YouTube , and TikTok ) to stay up to date on College Football 27. EA Play members can kick off their season in EA SPORTS™ College Football 27 with a 10-hour trial*, plus score a Welcome Pack and recurring monthly College Ultimate Team™ Packs. EA Play Pro members also get full access to the EA SPORTS™ College Football 27 Pro Edition, including the base game, early access solo challenges and 500 CUT Points every month for 12 months (6,000 total, through June 2028), and more. As always, EA Play members save 10% on EA digital purchases, including game downloads, pre-orders, Season Passes, College Football Points and downloadable content. Learn more at the EA Play website . *Conditions, limitations and exclusions apply. See tos.ea.com/legalapp/eaplay/US/en/PC/ for details. Check out other amazing EA stories on ea.com/news . Related News EA SPORTS™ presents Beckham, Zidane and Zlatan together for the first time. Electronic Arts Inc. title: hotglue melt: December 2025
summary: Improved job logs view, widget v3 updates, audit trail, and more!
body_text: 🚀 Product Updates 📖 Job Logs page updates We’ve refreshed the job details / logs page to give you more context about your jobs! Our goal was to improve the visibility into the job to make debugging various issues easier. The following information is now accessible directly in the job logs page: Compute Metrics → the provisioned resources and usage for your job Connector Versions → the connector versions (tag + repository) that ran in this job Overrides → job-level overrides Record-level target state → previously, visibility into each record that was synced to a target was limited. In addition to the count, you can now drill deeper and review each record, along with associated errors. If you have any feedback on the new job logs page, let us know! 🔨 Widget v3 updates In October we launched the new v3 Hotglue widget – since then we’ve been steadily adding more functionality! New features include: Support for file uploads Ability for tenants to trigger jobs and review job history Support for cloud file storage connectors like Google Drive and SharePoint To learn more about the v3 widget, check out the docs . 🕵️ Audit Trail We are excited to introduce an Audit Trail add-on to give you full visibility into what’s happening inside your Hotglue environment. When changes happen, it’s critical to know: Was this triggered by an end-user (tenant)? Someone on your internal team? Or programmatically via the API? With Audit Trail, you can now: See a chronological timeline of changes Identify exactly who (or what) initiated an action Quickly trace configuration updates, connection changes, and API-driven events No more guessing. No more “it worked yesterday.” Just a clear, searchable history directly inside Hotglue. 👉 Available as a paid add-on. Reach out if you'd like to try it out. 🔌 Connector Updates ⚡ BigQuery + Postgres target performance improvements We’ve rolled out major performance upgrades to both our BigQuery and Postgres targets — with significant speed gains across the board. 🟢 BigQuery: 5–10x Faster We’ve completely revamped how data is processed and loaded: Optimized JSON serialization & deserialization Faster JSON Schema validation Improved date parsing In-memory caching to reduce repeated computation New bulk loading flow: Data is first processed into Parquet files (one per stream) Files are uploaded to GCS BigQuery loads directly from GCS The result: dramatically faster and more reliable warehouse loads at scale. 🟢 Postgres: 3–10x Faster Postgres performance also saw major improvements: Optimized JSON serialization & deserialization Faster JSON Schema validation In-memory caching Removal of legacy features that were unused but impacting performance Net result: materially improved throughput, especially for high-volume syncs. That’s all for this month! Thanks for reading :) Want to chat with our team? Book a demo . TABLE OF CONTENTS 🚀 Product Updates 📖 Job Logs page updates 🔨 Widget v3 updates 🕵️ Audit Trail 🔌 Connector Updates ⚡ BigQuery + Postgres target performance improvements RECOMMENDED BLOGS Introducing the new and improved widget Announcing the brand new version of the widget, featuring enhanced performance, customizability, and a refreshed design. JavaScript & TypeScript Support for Hotglue Transforms Hotglue now supports writing transformation scripts in JavaScript or TypeScript in addition to Python! Optimizing Microsoft SQL insert speed in Python: pymssql vs. pyodbc vs. bcp Learn how we optimized our Microsoft SQL target by using bcp to boost insertion speed and switching from pymssql to pyodbc.
